content: The references provided are a comprehensive list of studies, reports, and guidelines related to HIV treatment, prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT), and antiretroviral therapy (ART) implementation across various global settings. 1. A study published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015 explored the role of viral therapy in the early asymptomatic stages of HIV infection, providing critical insights into treatment timing and outcomes. 2. Cohen, Chen, McCauley, and colleagues presented the final results of the HPTN 052 randomized controlled trial in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2015. This landmark study demonstrated that antiretroviral therapy (ART) effectively prevents HIV transmission among serodiscordant couples. 3. The Brazilian Ministry of Health released an epidemiological bulletin in 2014 addressing AIDS and sexually transmitted diseases (STDs), highlighting national trends and public health strategies. 4. Nsanzimana conducted a rapid assessment of Rwanda’s “test and treat” strategy for key populations, as part of the 2013 HIV treatment guidelines. This unpublished report from the Rwanda Biomedical Center in 2015 provided valuable data on the program’s implementation. 5. Kato, Long, Duong, and colleagues published findings in Current HIV/AIDS Reports in 2014, emphasizing the benefits of ART in Vietnam and its potential to contribute to the global goal of ending AIDS. 6. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidelines in 2015 on when to initiate ART and the use of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention, offering a public health approach to treatment. 7. Anglemyer, Rutherford, Easterbrook, and colleagues conducted a systematic review in 2014, published in AIDS, on the early initiation of ART in HIV-infected adults and adolescents, underscoring its clinical benefits. 8. Johnson, Sabin, and Girardi discussed the definition and epidemiology of late presentation of HIV in Europe in a 2010 article in Antiviral Therapy, providing a framework for addressing delayed diagnosis. 9. Geng, Hunt, Diero, and colleagues analyzed trends in the clinical characteristics of HIV-infected patients initiating ART in Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania between 2002 and 2009, as published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2011. 10. The HIV Modelling Consortium produced an unpublished report in 2015, outlining priorities for HIV care in sub-Saharan Africa from a population perspective. 11. UNAIDS released the Gap Report in 2014, providing a detailed analysis of the gaps in HIV prevention and treatment services globally. 12. Arreola, Santos, Beck, and colleagues examined the impact of sexual stigma, criminalization, and investment on access to HIV services among men who have sex with men worldwide, as published in AIDS Behavior in 2015. 13. Mahajan, Sayles, Patel, and colleagues reviewed the literature on stigma in the HIV/AIDS epidemic in a 2008 article in AIDS, offering recommendations for addressing this critical barrier to care. 14. Pulerwitz and Bongartz emphasized the importance of tackling stigma as a fundamental step toward an AIDS-free future in a 2014 article in The Lancet Global Health. 15. The Sustainable East Africa Research in Community Health (SEARCH) initiative provided insights into community-based HIV interventions, as accessed in 2015. 16. The MaxART Project, focusing on early access to ART for all, shared its progress and findings online in 2015. 17. The Botswana Combination Prevention Project (BCPP) highlighted its efforts in HIV prevention through a combination of strategies, as detailed on its website in 2015. 18. HPTN 071 (PopART) provided updates on its large-scale trial investigating the impact of universal testing and treatment on HIV incidence, as accessed in 2015. 19. The ANRS 12249 TasP Protocol outlined a trial on treatment as prevention in South Africa, with details available in a 2015 document. 20. The Global Plan towards the elimination of new HIV infections among children by 2015 and keeping their mothers alive (2011–2015) was a key initiative by UNAIDS, with resources available online. 21. The Kesho Bora Study Group conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing triple ART with zidovudine and single-dose nevirapine prophylaxis during pregnancy and breastfeeding for PMTCT, as published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2011. 22. Shapiro, Hughes, Ogwu, and colleagues investigated ART regimens during pregnancy and breastfeeding in Botswana, with findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2010. 23. Minnear, Girde, Angira, and colleagues analyzed outcomes among women who discontinued maternal triple ART regimens initially used for PMTCT in Kenya, as published in PLoS One in 2013. 24. Okonji, Zeh, Weidle, and colleagues studied CD4, viral load response, and adherence among ART-naive breastfeeding women receiving triple ART prophylaxis in Kisumu, Kenya, as published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012. 25. Thomas, Masaba, Borkowf, and colleagues conducted the Kisumu Breastfeeding Study, a clinical trial on triple ART prophylaxis for PMTCT through breastfeeding, as published in PLoS Medicine in 2011. 26. Ayuo, Musick, Liu, and colleagues examined adherence to and completion of combination ART for PMTCT in western Kenya, as published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2013. 27. Ekouevi, Abrams, Schlesinger, and colleagues reported on maternal CD4+ cell count decline after interruption of ART prophylaxis for PMTCT, as published in PLoS One in 2012. 28. Gartland, Chintu, Li, and colleagues evaluated the field effectiveness of combination ART prophylaxis for PMTCT in rural Zambia, as published in AIDS in 2013. 29. Giuliano, Andreotti, Liotta, and colleagues assessed maternal and infant outcomes two years after delivery among women receiving ART for PMTCT in Malawi, as published in PLoS One in 2013. 30. Linguissi, Bisseye, Sagna, and colleagues studied the efficiency of highly active ART (HAART) in preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission at a medical center in Burkina Faso, as published in the Asian Pacific Journal of Tropical Medicine in 2012. 31. Liotta, Mancinelli, Nielsen-Saines, and colleagues reported on the reduction of maternal mortality with HAART in a large cohort of HIV-infected pregnant women in Malawi and Mozambique, as published in PLoS One in 2013. 32. Phillips, Thebus, Bekker, and colleagues investigated disengagement from ART services among HIV-positive pregnant and postpartum women in South Africa, as published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2014. 33. Thistle, Bolotin, Schwarz, and colleagues studied the impact of HAART on PMTCT in rural Zimbabwe during a socio-economic crisis, as published in Medicine, Conflict, and Survival in 2011. 34. Ngemu, Khayeka-Wandabwa, Kweka, and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of Option B+ HAART for PMTCT in pregnant HIV-positive women, as published in BMC Research Notes in 2014. 35. Nyandiko, Otieno-Nyunya, Musick, and colleagues analyzed outcomes of HIV-exposed children in western Kenya, as published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2010. 36. Palombi, Galluzzo, Pirillo, and colleagues studied viro-immunological responses and resistance emergence in HIV-infected women receiving combination ART for PMTCT in Malawi, as published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2014. 37. Coulborn, Trivino Duran, Metcalf, and colleagues presented preliminary findings on a routine PMTCT Option B+ program in rural Malawi at the 7th International AIDS Society Conference in 2013. 38. Herce, Hosseinipour, van der Horst, and colleagues discussed the scale-up of Option B+ and comprehensive PMTCT service delivery in Malawi at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in 2015. 39. Kamuyango, Hirschhorn, Wang, and colleagues reviewed one-year outcomes of women starting ART during pregnancy before and after Option B+ implementation in Malawi, as published in the World Journal of AIDS in 2014. 40. Kim, Ahmed, Hosseinipour, and colleagues analyzed the impact of Option B+ on the antenatal PMTCT cascade in Lilongwe, Malawi, as published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2015. 41. Lu, Adler, Marston, and colleagues studied retention among HIV-infected pregnant women initiating lifelong ART (Option B+) in Haiti, as presented at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in 2015. 42. Namukwaya, Namara-Lugolobi, Mubiru, and colleagues shared early challenges in implementing Option B+ among women in Uganda at the 7th International AIDS Society Conference in 2013. 43. Price, Kayange, Zaba, and colleagues conducted a retrospective cohort study on the uptake of PMTCT using Option B+ in northern rural Malawi, as published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2014. 44. Speight, Phiri, Hosseinipour, and colleagues reported on the first 18 months of implementing Option B+ for PMTCT at Bwaila Maternity Unit in Lilongwe, as presented at the 7th International AIDS Society Conference in 2013. 45. Tenthani, Haas, Tweya, and colleagues studied retention in care under universal ART for HIV-infected pregnant and breastfeeding women (Option B+) in Malawi, as published in AIDS in 2014. 46. Tweya, Gugsa, Hosseinipour, and colleagues investigated factors and outcomes related to loss to follow-up among women in the Option B+ PMTCT program in Lilongwe, as published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2014. 47. Watts, Brown, Maldonado, and colleagues analyzed HIV disease progression in African women during the first year postpartum, as part of the HPTN 046 clinical trial, as published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2013. 48. Pilotte studied maternal outcomes after HAART for PMTCT in HIV-infected women in Brazil, as published in Antiretroviral Therapy in 2011. 49. Giuliano, Liotta, Andreotti, and colleagues assessed retention, transfer out, and loss to follow-up two years after delivery among HIV-positive pregnant women in Malawi, as published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2015. 50. Clouse, Pettifor, Shearer, and colleagues studied loss to follow-up before and after delivery among women testing HIV-positive during pregnancy in Johannesburg, as published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2013. 51. Ford, Mofenson, Shubber, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the safety of efavirenz during the first trimester of pregnancy, as published in AIDS in 2014. 52. O’Brien, Shaffer, Sangrujee, and colleagues analyzed the incremental cost of switching from Option B to Option B+ for PMTCT, as published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2014. 53. Gopalappa, Stover, Shaffer, and colleagues evaluated the costs and benefits of Option B+ for PMTCT, as published in AIDS in 2014. 54. Ishikawa, Shimbo, Miyano, and colleagues assessed the health outcomes and cost impact of the 2013 WHO guidelines on PMTCT in Zambia, as published in PLoS One in 2014. 55. Ngariina, Tarimo, Naburi, and colleagues explored women’s preferences regarding infant or maternal ART prophylaxis for PMTCT during breastfeeding in Tanzania, as published in PLoS One in 2014. 56. Hsieh, Mburu, Garner, and colleagues gathered community and service provider views to inform the 2013 WHO consolidated ART guidelines, as published in AIDS in 2014. 57. Myer, Phillips, Manuelli, and colleagues documented the evolution of ART services for HIV-infected pregnant women in Cape Town, as published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2015. 58. Tenthani, Haas, Tweya, and colleagues studied retention in care under universal ART for HIV-infected pregnant and breastfeeding women (Option B+) in Malawi, as published in AIDS in 2014. 59. Price, Kayange, Zaba, and colleagues conducted a retrospective cohort study on the uptake of PMTCT using Option B+ in northern rural Malawi, as published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2014. 60. Phillips, McNairy, Zerbe, and colleagues examined postpartum transfer of care among HIV-infected women initiating ART during pregnancy, as published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2015. 61. Woldesenbet, Jackson, Lombard, and colleagues identified missed opportunities along the PMTCT service cascade in South Africa, as published in PLoS One in 2015. 62. The Global Health Estimates 2013 report summarized disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years of life lost (YLLs), and years lived with disability (YLDs) by cause, age, and sex across WHO regions and World Bank income classifications.
